verdicts.quote: Promotion is **automatic**: when a spot opens, the first eligible waitlisted member is booked immediately, no offer to accept.
Waitlist order is first come, first served by the time the join was accepted. ... simultaneous joins ... resolve as if executed in some serial order ... Out of scope: ... paid or priority tiers
Waitlisting overlapping classes is allowed. ... If the head of the waitlist is no longer eligible to book when a spot opens, that entry is removed
verdicts.missing: Whether promotion into one class removes or otherwise resolves the member's entry in an overlapping class; overlap eligibility is left to G-6.

verdicts.quote: a member may be booked into a class they no longer want and must cancel under the normal cancellation rules.
verdicts.missing: The existing late-cancel/no-show policy is unknown (G-1); whether cancelling right after a late promotion incurs a penalty is not decided.

verdicts.quote: in the same atomic operation the first eligible entry is removed from the waitlist and booked ... join, leave and cancel complete synchronously, including promotion.
A notification is attempted through the channel chosen under G-3 stating class, date and time. ... a delivery failure never undoes the booking and is recorded
verdicts.missing: The notification channel (and final wording) is left open under G-3.

verdicts.quote: One spot promotes exactly one member. k spots promote the first k eligible entries in order. ... No member is promoted twice and no spot is double-assigned.
direct book | not booked to booked if free | `CLASS_FULL` offers waitlist; `ALREADY_BOOKED`; `ALREADY_WAITLISTED` ... resolve as if executed in some serial order
Joining the waitlist costs nothing and holds no credit or payment; any charge happens only at promotion, exactly as a normal booking would.
verdicts.missing: What happens when the charge at promotion fails (skip to next entry, remove, retry) is not stated; payment model unknown (G-6).

verdicts.quote: Waitlist cap (per class, per member) unspecified. No bound is invented. ... Treated as unbounded in the spec
verdicts.missing: Whether there is a cap and what a member sees when the waitlist is full remain open.

verdicts.quote: The waitlist closes at class start. Promotion happens up to class start; no earlier cutoff.
conditional on G-7: S-4, capacity 3 raised to 5, booked A, B, C, waitlist D, E, F, G: D and E are promoted
verdicts.missing: Lowering capacity while a waitlist exists is not addressed, and raising is conditional on the capability existing.

verdicts.quote: If the class is cancelled (existing staff action, G-7), all entries are removed and members notified together with booked members as today.

verdicts.where: State and data assessment, PD-1, R-2
verdicts.quote: Waitlist entry (class, member, join order, status) ... Member-surface display state (position, pending) | the client, transient | derived
at class start the waitlist is closed and its entries removed ... Left out: retaining history of waitlist entries beyond class start.
A member sees only their own position and the list length is not shown. ... A member never receives another member's identity, the other entries or the total length
Staff view of a waitlist (names, order) is not requested. ... Out of scope: staff-side waitlist management or roster
verdicts.missing: The topic is named but explicitly excluded; no staff view, manual promote/remove, or promotion audit view is specified.

verdicts.quote: in the same atomic operation the first eligible entry is removed from the waitlist and booked
booking a class with a free spot, cancelling a booking, listing classes and the capacity limit work as they do today.
Migration: waitlist entries are a new record; no existing record is migrated.
verdicts.missing: Whether classes already full at launch gain a waitlist (and how) is not stated explicitly.
